fullText:
Summary: Digital Mobility Solutions Lanka PLC (PickMe, PKME.N0000) is an excellent business: Sri Lanka's leading ride-hailing and delivery app, with no debt, a return on equity near 70% and profit up 49% in the six months to September 2026. At Rs 164.00 the share trades at 20.5x trailing earnings, which already prices in several more years of fast growth. Assuming growth slows from about 25% a year towards 6% over ten years, the methods put fair value at about Rs 131, so the price is about 25% above it. I'd buy at up to about Rs 111 and treat under Rs 98 as a strong buy.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 164.00 (CSE closing price, 2026-11-06). Please check it live. In July–September 2026 it traded between Rs 152.00 and Rs 173.00, and in April–June between Rs 134.75 and Rs 175.25. It closed the year to March 2026 at Rs 137.25, up from Rs 73.10 a year earlier.
Six months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited): revenue rose 38% to Rs 5.38bn and profit rose 49% to Rs 1.41bn. EPS was Rs 4.24 against Rs 2.85. The September quarter alone earned Rs 784mn (EPS Rs 2.35), the best quarter so far, even though fuel shortages held back the June quarter.
Activity: the value of trips and deliveries on the app (GTV) rose 43% to Rs 53.8bn in the half year. About 2.1mn people used the app each month in the September quarter (up 38%), and the number of drivers earning on it rose 58%.
Year to March 2026 (audited): revenue Rs 8.68bn (up 49%), profit Rs 2.20bn (up 88%), EPS Rs 6.61 (Rs 3.51), ROE 68.7%, dividends Rs 4.30 (65% of profit), free cash flow about Rs 2.5bn.
Balance sheet: no borrowings apart from office leases, and Rs 4.0bn in cash and short-term investments at September 2026 (about Rs 12 a share). NAV is Rs 13.34.
Dividend: an interim dividend of Rs 2.75 was declared for this year (65% of half-year profit).
History: EPS Rs 2.05 (2023/24), Rs 3.51 (2024/25), Rs 6.61 (2025/26). Listed on the CSE in October 2024.

Methods
NAV (Rs 13.34): 12.3x. Not useful here: the business needs very little capital, so its value is in its earnings, not its assets.
Return on equity: 68.7% in 2025/26 (54% and 49% in the two years before).
P/E: 20.5x trailing EPS of Rs 8.00. Year-end P/E: 20.8x (2026), 20.8x (2025).
Dividends: Rs 4.30 for 2025/26, a 2.6% yield; 65% payout.
Cash-flow DCF (free cash flow about Rs 8.7 a share this year, growth fading over 10 years): Rs 83.7 / 148.4 / 237.5, weighted Rs 146.8.
P/E method: Rs 104.4 / 148.8 / 194.0, weighted Rs 144.5.
Dividend model: Rs 58.6 / 102.3 / 162.6, weighted Rs 101.3.

PickMe turns nearly all its profit into free cash, so a cash-flow DCF suits it; residual income adds little because the book value is so small. The dividend model is the strictest because about a third of profit is kept, mostly as cash. The DCF has the widest range because the value depends heavily on how long fast growth lasts.

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity: 17.5% / 16% / 15%.
Growth in the first year, fading to long-term growth over 10 years: 15% / 25% / 32%.
Long-term growth: 5% / 6% / 7%.
Free cash flow this year (Rs a share): 8.0 / 8.7 / 9.2.
EPS for the year to March 2027 × P/E: 8.7 × 12 / 9.3 × 16 / 9.7 × 20.
Dividend this year (Rs a share): 5.6 / 6.0 / 6.3.
Average of the three methods: Rs 82.2 / Rs 133.2 / Rs 198.0.
Common: Sri Lankan 7–10-year government bonds yield about 12% (October 2026). In the base case the second half of this year grows about 35% on last year's, giving EPS of about Rs 9.30 for the year to March 2027.

Fair value and buy price
Fair value: weighting 30/50/20 gives about Rs 131 (about 16x trailing earnings), so Rs 164.00 is about 25% above it.
Buy price: a 15% margin of safety gives Rs 111.40, and 25% gives Rs 98.30.
Plan for 500 shares: 200 at up to Rs 131.00, 150 at up to Rs 111.40 and 150 at up to Rs 98.30. That averages about Rs 115.31, about Rs 57,655, against Rs 82,000 at Rs 164.00.
Realism: Rs 131 needs about a 20% fall. The share got close (Rs 134.75) in April–June 2026 and fell to Rs 127.25 in January–March 2026, so the first tier is realistic. Rs 111 and below would probably need a market sell-off or a growth scare.

Sensitivity (DCF base case, Rs per share)
Cost of equity 14.5%: 133.3 / 177.8 / 235.8 for first-year growth of 15% / 25% / 35%.
Cost of equity 16%: 112.2 / 148.4 / 195.2.
Cost of equity 17.5%: 96.7 / 126.8 / 165.6.
Value is very sensitive to how long fast growth lasts.

What would change my view
Supports a higher value: growth staying above 30% for longer; food and grocery delivery adding profit; lower interest rates; a higher payout or special dividends from the cash pile.
Supports a lower value: a strong competitor (such as Uber) cutting prices; fuel shortages or new rules on ride-hailing or driver pay; growth slowing sharply; much higher spending on new services; higher taxes on digital services.

These are my estimates from the annual reports for the years to March 2025 and March 2026 and the interim reports to September 2026. The interim figures are unaudited, so check the price before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.
